text:
maya (support): FYI — Customer AuroraAI opened a ticket: sudden 5xx spike and high tail latency, they say traffic is landing in us-east even for EU users. link: https://support.internal/t/1324 :thinking_face:
elaine (sre): can you paste an example trace and a client IP?
maya (support): pasted from the trace (redacted):
```
client_ip: 80.79.64.12
x-edge-pop: us-east-1
x-request-id: r-9a8b7c
response: 502 / 0.5-3s tail latency
```
samir (infra): that IP range looks like an ISP transparent proxy in DE — often strips EDNS/Client-Subnet. If EDNS gets stripped we can get faraway DNS answers.
marco (eng-infra): +1. Any dig from the customer's resolver? maya, do we have the DNS answers recorded?
maya (support): yes, grabbed from packet capture (customer-side resolver):
```
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;api.redwood.example. IN A
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.example. 30 IN A 3.5.21.12  ; us-east
```
aurora-customer: Confirming — AWS eu-west users were hitting us-east IPs, saw higher latency and intermittent auth 401s. Billing report shows increased egress and model fallback to paid hosted variant. Not good.
elaine (sre): auth 401s could be from region mismatch hitting a control-plane that doesn't have synced keys for their dedicated tenant. Need to confirm key sync state.
marco (eng-infra): running fast probe across a handful of resolvers now. probe-bot will post results. :mag_right:
probe-bot: quick probe results:
```
resolver 84.16.0.1: strips EDNS -> A 3.5.21.12 (us-east)
resolver 8.8.8.8: preserves EDNS -> A 54.36.87.10 (eu-west)
resolver 185.37.12.5: strips EDNS -> A 3.5.21.12 (us-east)
TTL returned: 30s
```
samir (infra): there it is — several ISP resolvers are stripping EDNS which causes inconsistent answers and low TTLs. That explains stale cache oscillation and sticky misroutes.
maya (support): customer asks for repro steps to show vendor/ISP.
marco (eng-infra): repro instructions (customer can run these):
```
# compare resolver behavior
dig @<their-resolver> +edns=0 +noall +answer api.redwood.example
# then test with a public resolver
dig @8.8.8.8 +edns=0 +noall +answer api.redwood.example
# capture the authority/AD bits and TTLs
```
elaine (sre): mitigation options while we engage ISP:
- pin customer to eu model endpoint via our routing override (temporary)
- increase our routing TTL tolerance and add hard preference for eu variants for their org id
- disable cross-region fallback for their tenant (prevents unexpected egress/billing)
(can do 1-2 as short-term)
samir (infra): I'll check geoip DB version and whether our authoritative DNS is emitting ECS hints. If authoritative is not emitting ECS and relies on downstream EDNS, that worsens.
aurora-customer: would appreciate steps we can show ISP. They keep saying it's our CDN.
marco (eng-infra): include this in ISP ticket: show dig outputs (two resolvers) and router-level packet capture showing EDNS absent. Also show repeated A answers for different resolvers.
maya (support): opening escalation to eng-infra + SRE. Action items:
- samir: confirm if authoritative is sending ECS/EDNS options and timestamp (ETA 2h)
- marco: roll a routing override for org aurora-ai to prefer eu (ETA 30m)
- elaine: check token/key sync for their dedicated tenant (ETA 1h)
- maya: provide customer repro steps and a short summary for ISP (ETA 15m)
elaine (sre): note: if we flip routing override, watch for cache TTL collisions — set override with short TTL and monitor.
probe-bot: background probe after 10m: still seeing ~40% of sampled resolvers strip EDNS and return us-east.
deploy-bot: routing override for org:aurora-ai scheduled and applied (id ro-773) — rolled back earlier test flag to avoid wider impact. :white_check_mark:
samir (infra): geoip DB is up-to-date (2026-02-28) and authoritative is emitting ECS in our responses, so this is definitely resolver-side stripping.
aurora-customer: thanks team. after override latency dropped from 800ms tail to ~80ms and 401s stopped. we'll keep ISP ticket open.
marco (eng-infra): long-term follow-ups:
- add resolver classification telemetry to detect EDNS-stripping resolvers and auto-apply local geo overrides per org
- add clearer billing protections when cross-region fallback triggers due to DNS anomalies
- include a one-click customer-facing repro pack for ISP escalation
maya (support): noted. closing loop with Aurora once we have ISP response. :pray:
elaine (sre): reassign to postmortems if this recurs. :eyes:
